title: Introduce severity-weighted failure classifier and progressive CI attenuator
author: Asha Menon
description: Motivation: CI for prompt-set regressions currently treats all failing prompts as equal which causes noisy hard-blocks for low-impact regressions and noisy signal for triage. This PR introduces a severity-weighted failure classifier (SVFC) that: 1) assigns a contextual severity score to individual prompt-set failures (low/medium/high based on topicality, token-impact, downstream metric delta and historical flakiness), 2) aggregates a severity-adjusted regression rate metric used in CI decisions, and 3) plugs into a progressive CI attenuator that can soften CI enforcement for low-severity regressions while keeping high-severity failures blocking. What changed: added a new classifier and supporting feature flags, an integration point in the CI eval hook that emits a severity breakdown annotation on PRs, a new evaluation metric severityAdjustedRegressionRate surfaced in test reports and dashboards, CI policy configuration with default thresholds (low=0.05, medium=0.02, high=0.005 fraction), a small sample prompt-sensitivity dataset for unit/regression tests, and docs on how teams can tune attenuation behavior per repo or per prompt-cohort. Design considerations and tradeoffs: classifier uses a compact heuristic model (logistic blend of token-level delta, semantic-change score, and historical flakiness) to keep latency minimal; full ML-backed models are out of scope for this change but can be layered later. The progressive attenuator implements a leaky-quarantine pattern: low-severity failing prompts are flagged and counted towards a quarantined bucket that will delay block escalations for a configurable grace window, while medium/high severity still trigger quicker review. Backwards compatibility: feature gated off by default; default policy is conservative (blocks on medium+ by default) so existing CI behavior is preserved until teams opt-in. Related: ENG-4289 (ev-harness quality gates), SUP-3412 (support ticket on noisy prompt CI blocks).
commits_summary: 4 commits: initial severity classifier prototype and unit tests; add CI hook and annotation renderer; integrate severityAdjustedRegressionRate in reporter; docs and config defaults; follow-up tweak to default thresholds after reviewer feedback.
review_comments: Jordan Lee: Nice isolation of the classifier logic. Two asks: (1) can the default thresholds be more conservative or at least clearly documented in the config file? (2) add an explicit test that shows quarantined low-severity failures do not block when the grace window is active.
Asha Menon: Addressed both: bumped the default low threshold documentation and added test 'test_quarantine_grace_window' and a short note in docs clarifying opt-in behavior.
Priya Kapur: Question on metrics — severityAdjustedRegressionRate looks useful but how does it correlate with existing regressionRate? Please add a small migration note for dashboards.
Asha Menon: Added migration note in docs and a helper function in severity_reporter to emit both raw and adjusted rates for easy dashboard mapping.
Elliot Samuels: CI flakiness spike observed on first run (integration smoke) due to randomness in the sample dataset; recommend seeding and making the sample deterministic.
Asha Menon: Seeded the sample generator and re-ran CI; all flaky tests stabilized.
ci_checks: integration-smoke: initial run failed (flaky sample), rerun passed
merge_outcome: merged (squash) by Jordan Lee after approvals from Priya Kapur and Elliot Samuels; branch deleted. Notes: feature gated off by default and rollout flagged for gradual opt-in in release notes and console feature-flags UI.
release_notes: Add severity-weighted failure classification and progressive CI attenuator; New metric severityAdjustedRegressionRate; CI annotations show severity breakdown on PRs; Feature-gated and opt-in per-repo; Includes sample prompt-sensitivity dataset and tests; Docs for tuning thresholds and migration notes.
notes_for_adopters: Opt-in steps: enable 'severity-attenuator' feature flag for your repo, tune thresholds in examples/ci-configs/attenuator-defaults.yaml, run the provided sample suite to see annotations, and monitor 'severityAdjustedRegressionRate' in dashboards. Recommended default behavior is to allow teams to run in passive mode (annotations only) for two weeks before enabling active attenuation.
